entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Applicant :- Ashish Rai,Om Prakash Rai Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Surya Pratap Singh Hon'ble Vipin Chandra Dixit,J.

Heard Sri Ashish Rai, learned counsel for the applicants, learned AGA for the State, Sri Yashdeep Rastogi, Advocate holding brief of Sri Surya Pratap Singh, learned counsel for opposite party no.2 and perused the record.

It is submitted by learned counsel for applicants that it is a matrimonial dispute between the parties and parties had settled their dispute amicably outside the Court and a written compromise has taken place between the parties on 13.9.2021.
Copy of compromise is annexed as Annexure-5 to the affidavit filed in support of application.
The opposite party no.2 does not want to prosecute the applicants.
This Court vide order dated 8.4.2022 directed the parties to appear before the trial court for verification of compromise.

sentences.text: As per report of A.C.J.M./Additional Civil Judge (S.D.)-Ist, Ghaziabad dated 9.5.2022, parties had appeared before the Court below on 2.5.2022 in compliance of order dated 8.4.2022 and filed copy of compromise for its verification.
Both the parties were identified by their respective counsels and the compromise was verified by the Court below.
Learned AGA for the State and learned counsel for opposite party no.2 do not dispute the aforesaid facts.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of State of Madhya Pradesh Vs. Laxmi Narayan and others,
reported in (2019) 5 SCC 688 has laid down principles for quashing the proceeding on the basis of settlement/compromise.

sentences.text:
Relevant paragraph no.15 is quoted hereinbelow:-
"15.
However, the High Court would not rest its decision merely because there is a mention of Section 307 IPC in the FIR or the charge is framed under this provision.

It would be open to the High Court to examine as to whether incorporation of Section 307 IPC is there for the sake of it or the prosecution has collected sufficient evidence, which if proved, would lead to framing the charge under Section 307 IPC.

For this purpose, it would be open to the High Court to go by the nature of injury sustained, whether such injury is inflicted on the vital/delegate parts of the body,
Ayush Tyagi And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191458287/
2 nature of weapons used etc.

entities.text: Ayush Tyagi And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, such an exercise by the High Court would be permissible only after the evidence is collected after investigation and the charge sheet is filed/charge is framed and/or during the trial.
Such exercise is not permissible when the matter is still under investigation.

In view of the aforesaid fact, since the parties have amicably settled their dispute outside the Court and compromise between the parties had already been verified by the Court below, the present application U/s 482 Cr.P.C. is liable to be allowed.

Accordingly, the present application U/s 482 Cr.P.C. is allowed and the proceedings of Case No.1057 of 2021 (State Vs. Ayush and others), arising out of Case Crime No.093 of 2021, under Sections 323,
498A, 504, 506, 342 I.P.C., P.S. Nandgram, District Ghaziabad, is hereby quashed.
